t: You're at the site of Grove Hill House, a house in Southwark. It was commissioned and owned by John Coakley Lettsom, who lived from 1744 to 1815. Lettsom was a physician and philanthropist, born in a Quaker settlement in the British Virgin Islands, and he grew up to be an abolitionist. In 1773 he founded the Medical Society of London, the oldest society of its kind in the United Kingdom. He was its mainstay as founder, president and benefactor.
